Joining Acme

This page describes exactly how our engineering interview process runs. We publish it because an interview where only one side knows the format is a test of guessing, not of engineering.

1. Intro call (30 minutes)

A conversation with the hiring manager about what you have built and what you want to build next. No code. We will ask why logistics, and "the problem sounded interesting" is a fine answer.

2. Take-home exercise (three hours, paid)

You receive a file of messy carrier tracking events and are asked to reconcile them into one ordered shipment timeline, handling duplicate and contradictory events. We pay for your time and we cap it at three hours — if it takes longer, stop and tell us what you would have done next.

3. Take-home review (60 minutes)

We read your submission before the call. You walk us through the trade-offs, and we push on the edges you chose not to handle. We are looking for whether you can defend a decision and change your mind when given a better argument.

4. System design (60 minutes)

An open design session on a problem close to what we actually run: ingesting several million events a day from unreliable third-party feeds, with ordering and idempotency requirements. Expect to talk about backpressure, replay and what happens when a carrier silently changes their schema.

5. Values conversation (45 minutes)

Two people you have not met ask about collaboration, disagreement and mentoring. We ask everyone the same questions.
